Definition: Amalek, a descendant of Esau; also his posterity and their country
BiblicalUsage: Amalek, the grandson of Esau through Eliphaz, and his people are Israel's first enemy after the Red Sea. Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim, and Joshua discomfited him with the edge of the sword while Moses held up his hands; and Moses commands Israel to remember what Amalek did by the way, when they were come forth out of Egypt, how he smote the hindmost, the feeble, all that were behind.
TheologicalSignificance: A name that is both a man and a people carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the enmity that runs through the whole story, that Amalek struck the weak at the back of the column, and the LORD swore war with Amalek from generation to generation.
